bluf: Hibu is a Cedar Rapids, IA local marketing platform company, PE backed by H.I.G. Capital and founded 2013, selling all in one, done for you marketing to local businesses through Hibu One: websites, listings, reviews, ad campaigns and automation. The record shows it practising what it sells, with 813 Google ads and 24 LinkedIn company ads, and moving AI search inside the platform. The one thing a rival should know: 6 of its 12 clients on record are names only and the Monsoon read is Landfall at 75.3, so it is very likely that its local book buys on price and can be undercut line by line.
doing:
Hibu positions itself as all in one, done for you digital marketing for local businesses through the Hibu One platform: in plain words, a subscription bundle of website, listings, reviews, ad campaigns and automation that the owner does not run. Its headline claim is decades of proprietary local business data, quoted as a claim, plus the 2024 Microsoft Advertising Channel Partner of the Year award, dated from its own news page.

The mix is ten services centred on the platform. Local leads at 3: the title sells digital marketing for local businesses and listings, reviews and reputation management lead the platform. Three core lines score 2: Email & CRM (the platform automates email and text outreach; news reports buying Signpost's marketing automation software business), Paid Search (ad campaigns on Google and more plus the Microsoft award) and Web & Product (copy leads with a website built and maintained for the client). SEO alone scores 1. Proprietary products: Hibu One, Business Listings Scan, Digital Marketing Score and Social Advertising Calculator. Partners: the Microsoft Advertising channel partnership and Intuit Gold Partner status with a QuickBooks Online integration.

Its AI posture sits inside the product: Hibu One markets AI and predictive targeting as its optimization engine and its SEO now includes AI search optimization for local visibility; AI Search / GEO and AI Automation / Agents each score 1.

Moves run from the 2024 Microsoft award to the Selling Power 60 Best Companies to Sell For listing in 2026-07, its ninth straight year. The news page adds the RevLocal acquisition and enhanced Google Business Profile optimization (record dated 2025-03-20), Gartner Digital Markets recognition for reviews and reputation, and Intuit Gold Partner status on 2025-11-21. Pricing: the nav links a Platform Pricing page; no figures were captured. Absent: no jobs on record, Content & Digital PR and CRO at 0, and no case study describing the method behind its lead counts.
clients:
The Radar marks Hibu's client type as local and its home market as the US, served from Cedar Rapids, IA, the only office listed. Verticals: Home services, Automotive, Healthcare and dental, Legal, Insurance, Accounting and tax, Pet care and veterinary, and Franchise.

The needs read counts 12 clients from 5 case studies and 7 slugs: 6 observed and 6 names only. All six observed needs are local and lead generation, the whole mix at 1.0, but the signal varies. Dixon Electric ('866 Leads in 90 Days') and Rembrandt Roofing & Restoration ('Gets 302 Leads') state a lead count. Lacey Denture Clinic, Main Heating & Air Conditioning and Keefer Wood Allen & Rahal carry titles naming a vertical ('Dental', 'HVAC', 'Employment Law Firm') plus digital marketing, not the work. Hildebrand Law Firm's title names only the client, the thinnest code in the book.

The names only are Wilcox & Reynolds Insurance, West Toledo Animal Hospital, Delta Pest Services, AAA Sewer Service and Levine Painting ('Hibu Client Case Study' titles) and Columbus Auto Body (an 'Auto Body Shop Case Study' title), their need inferred from the local lead line. The split is soft: that title reads names only while the HVAC title, built the same way, is coded.

No client sits on another tracked agency's book; the deepen pass counts 27 case studies, more than the read carries.

Horus has Hibu best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers): it is likely, moderate confidence, that these owners ask next to be found in AI answers and Local Services Ads, work already evidenced under P3. Under KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two), the paid social and display hours in the bundle have a roughly even chance of being questioned first.
house: The one say and do test is practised: Paid Search is corroborated by its own Google ads, 813 in the Transparency Center, 20 in the last 30 days. The Radar flags no gaps. It publishes an llms.txt, blocks no AI crawlers, and the sitemap lists 1063 URLs with 14 updated in 90 days and 399 in 365, with 2 AI URLs found. The tag stack is gtm, linkedin_insight, vwo and onetrust with no CMS identified, LinkedIn Insight the only pixel and VWO the test tool. Its Google Ads Transparency Center record shows 813 ads, 65 text, 696 image and 52 video, last shown 2026-09-27, under Yellow Book USA, Inc and A La Cart Catering LLC; one sample reads "Get Found By More Customers". Its LinkedIn record shows 24 company ads and 0 thought leader ads, a floor; one sample reads "The best thing about marketing is not having to think about it". No Meta or TikTok check is recorded.
market:
The Horus read puts Hibu at a tailwind index of 10.9, band Favored. It is best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) at net 0.175, driven by AI Search / GEO and Paid Search, and for KJ2 (ads inside AI answers) at 0.175; it is most exposed to KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two) at -0.09, driven by Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV, and to KJ4. The best scenario fit is The Walled Oasis at 47/100. It is making P3 (LSAs and Sponsored Places), P4 (inputs for automation) and P7 (owned audience hedges); P1 (audited AI visibility) is partial; P2, P6 and P8 are absent; P5 unknown.

The Monsoon read is 75.3, band Landfall, migration 69.3 against displacement 81.3, inferred from three terms: PE backed, local ICP and a scaled segment. 61 of the index is the sold mix, Local (17) and Web & Product (12) most movable; the shore split sends 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. No hub office or onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is price. Displacement 81.3 on the Monsoon read, a local ICP and PE ownership make it very likely, with moderate confidence (an inferred read), that the book buys on price and an offshore delivered rival can undercut the website, listings and review hours line by line. The falsifier is a captured Platform Pricing page showing outcome priced tiers.

The evidence gap to lead with is the book: 6 of 12 clients are names without described work, so a rival bringing a described local lead method to Wilcox & Reynolds Insurance, West Toledo Animal Hospital or Delta Pest Services can ask what the work was; those conversations are likely open. The described results, 866 leads in 90 days for Dixon Electric and 302 for Rembrandt Roofing, set the number to beat.

The move gaps: P8 absent, no ads inside AI assistants despite a paid search core, so the first local agency with results there sets the price; P2 absent, no feed, schema or entity work on a core local and web line; P1 partial, AI search optimization sold inside the bundle with no audited citation product, so an audited local AI visibility number likely wins that conversation.
watch: Indicator I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the search campaigns in its bundle, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and its AI search bet.

Indicator I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk behind KJ1.

Indicator I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the $2B milestone and pricing below $20 CPM would tell whether ads inside AI answers reach a local business budget before it moves on P8.

Follow up the dated moves: the Selling Power listing of 2026-07-13 and case studies updated through 2026-09-21 show a live publishing machine, so a slowdown from 14 sitemap updates in 90 days would be the first sign of change.
The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients; this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile.
